comparison: Perfect agreement on C104. Both evaluations support the structural observation about nucleotides 2652-2689 and 2816-2830. Peer reviewers request better visualization but accept the quality of the density maps.

Disagreement on forward-looking predictions (C76-C80). OpenEval considers these speculative claims requiring validation, while peer reviewers enthusiastically support the broader impact predictions, stating the work will 'revolutionize cryo-EM.'

Disagreement on data processing workflow (C65-C67, C70). OpenEval finds the particle numbers and classification results well-supported, while peer reviewers request additional methodological details about classification parameters.

Disagreement on methodological development (C100-C103). OpenEval finds the statistical framework clearly described with specific parameters, while peer reviewers request clarification on prior width selection and optimization procedures.
Agreement on detector capabilities (C7, C8, C34, C36, C37). Both evaluations accept the technical specifications and superior performance of direct electron detectors without challenge.

Agreement on beam-induced movement observations (C53, C58-C60). Both evaluations accept the movement data, though peer reviewers request clearer visualization to avoid false impressions about particle displacement magnitude.

Disagreement on movement pattern analysis (C55-C57, C61). OpenEval finds the experimental data in Figures 1-2 directly supportive, while peer reviewers question how time-dependent movement effects were accounted for.

Disagreement on experimental parameters (C48-C50, C96-C97). OpenEval finds data collection parameters clearly documented, while peer reviewers request clarification on beam tilt measurements and potential resolution limitations.

Agreement on comparative achievement claims (C71-C72, C74). Both evaluations support the resolution improvement and particle efficiency gains. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'impressive result' and 'new territory' for single-particle methods.

Agreement on core methodological results (C62-C64). Both evaluations support the demonstration of improvement through FSC curves, crystal structure comparison, and visual inspection. Peer reviewers describe the achievement as bringing resolution 'into a new territory.'

Agreement on prior work characterization (C38-C39). Both evaluations accept the authors' description of Brilot et al. and Campbell et al. studies showing limited resolution improvement with frame-by-frame alignment.

Disagreement on scope expansion claim (C9). OpenEval considers the broader implications speculative pending validation on diverse specimens, while peer reviewers enthusiastically support the achievement as documented.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background claims (C1-C5, C11-C32) about cryo-EM history and technical limitations as well-supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/introduction claims.

OpenEval evaluated ribosome properties and cryo-EM challenges (C40-C47) as accurately describing established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval found claims about current limitations and proposed strategies (C81-C89) to be partially speculative, with strategies not experimentally validated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion points.
OpenEval considered future impact predictions (C90-C92) as speculative, noting validation only on two ribosome systems. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these concluding predictions.
